correctness.rationale: After Steiner centering, constant width leaves exactly odd Fourier modes n>=3 and the area deficit is (pi/2) times the weighted coefficient energy. Weighted Cauchy--Schwarz for the two-point evaluation functional gives the claimed series; the odd-mode series evaluates to M(d)=(1-cos d)/2+(pi/2-d)sin d, with d=pi recovering the 2pi Hausdorff coefficient. For odd q-fold symmetry only frequencies q(2k+1) survive, and the reciprocal-weight sum is pi/(4q) tan(pi/(2q)), yielding 2q cot(pi/(2q)). The finite Fourier truncations in the package can be scaled so h+h remains positive and their ratios converge to the displayed constants, so finite computation is only corroborative, not the infinite proof.
risks: The claimed kernel identity is Fourier-analytic and valid at the natural H^1 support-function regularity; no hidden smoothness assumption is needed because smooth convolution/truncation gives the limiting argument.
